Why: a || b returns a if it is truthy, else b. a && b returns a if it is falsy, else b. a ?? b returns b only when a is null or undefined, so 0 ?? "zero" is 0.

Docs: MDN — Logical OR (||) — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/Logical_OR
notes.quote: However, the || operator actually returns the value of one of the specified operands, so if this operator is used with non-Boolean values, it will return a non-Boolean value.
